Neither global least-favorable/optimal interval geometry nor a strict-gap/equality optimized marginal-product comparison was delivered, and independent validity review confirms terminal kernel substitution with no supported bounded repair. tldr: A weak treatment-induced mediator shift multiplies a response contrast learned from finitely many discordant mediator observations. The scaled causal target tends to \(h(u-v)/2\), and its joint limit experiment contains a Gaussian shift and Bernoulli-marked Poisson counts with unknown intensities. Uniform two-way reconstruction and exact-honesty transfer give \(L_n\to L\), an original-data interval sequence attaining this limit, and an all-procedure converse. Contact-safe finite decision programs compute \(L\) and the optimized independently calibrated marginal-product value \(L_{\mathrm{prod}}\) to any prescribed certified accuracy over the full nuisance box. The certified comparison is \(b_\star\le L\le L_{\mathrm{prod}}\le0.45\), with \(b_\star>0.41472\), so \(0\le\Delta<0.03528\). Strict positivity of \(\Delta\) and global optimal interval geometry remain open. The exploratory value \(0.41944248\) failed off-grid honesty and is not a continuum upper certificate.
gap: Regular interventional mediation inference and optimal Gaussian product-zero tests do not determine the maximal expected length of honest intervals when rare joint cells leave a finite response experiment. Generic confidence-game optimization does not decide whether independently calibrated marginal products lose precision after both marginal rules and their coverage split have been optimized.
fill: The substantive target is the strict joint-calibration theorem, supported by an exact finite zero-fiber dual anchor, allocation-boundary inequalities, a globally certified independent-kernel polynomial program, a contact-safe direct interval program, and two-way exact-honesty transfer. No fixed marginal split, known intensity, or saved exploratory LP rule licenses the comparison.
